practiceNotes: Spaced retrieval maintains concepts, representations, assumptions and method selection; it does not certify proof-writing, software construction, laboratory technique or field performance.
Assess extended work separately through unseen problems, proof portfolios, tested code, raw data, notebooks, uncertainty analysis, oral defense and revision.

Laboratory, field and hardware activities require appropriate facilities, training, supervision and local risk assessment. Archived or synthetic data can support analysis but cannot certify hands-on technique.

Human-participant research, identifiable genomic data, animal work, genetic interventions and environmental sampling require applicable consent, ethics review and permissions; these conditions are not assumed satisfied.

Use nonpathogenic organisms, safer chemical substitutions and low-energy apparatus where possible. Radiation, high-power lasers, pressure systems and hazardous chemicals require specialist supervision.
Security exercises require explicit authorization and isolated systems. Autonomous robot tests require containment and independent safety review.
A provided-tool outcome assesses model specification, settings, interpretation and validation. Algorithm implementation and proof outcomes require separate learner-produced work.
Completion does not authorize clinical practice, hazardous synthesis, radiation handling or other regulated professional activity.

Derive retarded potentials and dipole radiation, calculate angular power and express Maxwell equations/transformations in locally taught covariant tensor notation.

practice: Derive a waveguide mode and radiating-source field, checking boundaries, gauge consistency and energy.

includes: Quantum approximation, angular momentum, scattering and composite states

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Solve quantum problems beyond introductory models.
decks.title: Graduate Quantum Mechanics

outcomes.description: Derive variational, WKB, degenerate and time-dependent perturbation methods; combine angular momenta and solve central potentials using taught Frobenius methods.
Calculate Born/partial-wave scattering; construct bosonic/fermionic states and density matrices; analyze reduced states, entanglement and measurement statistics.

practice: Compare variational and numerical bound states and calculate scattering with approximation-validity checks.

includes: Grand ensembles, quantum gases and phase transitions

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Analyze quantum populations and collective thermal behavior.
decks.title: Quantum Statistical Physics

outcomes.description: Derive Bose/Fermi occupations from state counting; calculate blackbody, degenerate-gas and condensation observables and thermodynamic limits.
Derive mean-field/Landau ordering models, analyze correlations and critical scaling and implement Metropolis sampling with detailed-balance and finite-size checks.

practice: Compare a sampled spin transition with mean-field predictions and calculate quantum-gas thermodynamics with numerical error control.

includes: Nuclear models, decay, reactions and particle detector evidence

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Connect subatomic models with observable evidence.
decks.title: Nuclear and Particle Physics

outcomes.description: Calculate binding, decay chains, tunneling and reaction Q-values using liquid-drop, shell and barrier models; distinguish fission, fusion and decay.
Apply conservation, invariant mass and cross-section definitions to reactions; interpret tracking, calorimetry and counts with taught efficiency, Poisson and background models.

practice: Reconstruct a resonance from simulated events and test efficiency and background explanations.

includes: Crystals, bands, phonons, transport, magnetism and soft matter

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Predict material behavior from microscopic structure.
decks.title: Condensed Matter Physics

outcomes.description: Construct reciprocal lattices/zones, derive one-dimensional nearly-free and tight-binding bands and apply taught Fermi occupation/density-of-states models to metals and semiconductors.
Calculate phonons, heat capacities and Drude transport; analyze bounded spin, elastic and polymer-chain models and interpret magnetic, liquid-crystalline and superconducting evidence.

practice: Infer material parameters from diffraction, heat-capacity and conductivity data and identify microscopic-model failures.

includes: Viscous incompressible flow, vorticity, boundary layers and computation

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Derive and validate continuum fluid predictions.
decks.title: Fluid Dynamics

outcomes.description: Derive continuity and Newtonian Navier-Stokes equations in Cartesian/tensor-component form; nondimensionalize, derive vorticity balances and solve Couette, Poiseuille, creeping and boundary-layer examples.

Implement a bounded two-dimensional incompressible projection solver with pressure boundary conditions; validate divergence, conservation, grid error and flow-regime assumptions against benchmark and laboratory data.

practice: Solve a viscous-flow benchmark and compare a two-dimensional computation with measured velocity or pressure data.

includes: Plasma scales, particle motion, screening and cold-fluid waves

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Predict basic collective charged-particle behavior.
decks.title: Plasma Physics

outcomes.description: Calculate gyration and guiding-center drifts; derive Debye screening using a taught Boltzmann-density closure and identify quasineutrality, collision and magnetization regimes.

Derive cold-fluid continuity/momentum closures and linear plasma oscillation and magnetized-wave dispersion; infer density and temperature from supplied probe/microwave models with sheath and calibration limitations.

practice: Analyze archived probe and wave data and distinguish screening, collisional and collective interpretations.

includes: Einstein equations, relativistic matter, Schwarzschild geometry and gravitational waves

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Calculate gravitation as spacetime dynamics.
decks.title: General Relativity

outcomes.description: Construct particle/perfect-fluid stress-energy tensors, derive geodesics variationally and apply Einstein equations and covariant conservation to symmetric metrics.
Calculate Schwarzschild redshift, precession, deflection and horizon properties; derive linearized gravitational waves and detector strain.

practice: Derive two observable relativistic corrections and analyze curvature and causal behavior near a horizon.

includes: Stellar structure, radiative transfer, compact objects and quantitative cosmology

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Build quantitative stellar and expansion models.
decks.title: Stellar and Cosmological Physics

outcomes.description: Derive/integrate spherical stellar mass, pressure, luminosity and temperature equations with stated opacity/nuclear rates; solve one-dimensional radiative transfer and analyze degenerate support.
Apply stated Friedmann equations and equations of state to expansion, distances and horizons; fit bounded cosmologies and assess degeneracy without claiming an Einstein-equation derivation.

practice: Implement stellar shooting and compare expansion-distance models with archival data using a supplied least-squares tool.

includes: Distributions, Sobolev spaces, energy estimates and numerical convergence theory

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Establish field-equation solvability and approximation guarantees.
decks.title: Advanced PDE Methods

outcomes.description: Define distributions, weak derivatives and Sobolev spaces; derive weak forms and energy estimates and prove representative elliptic existence/uniqueness and parabolic stability.
Prove finite-difference stability/convergence and finite-element coercivity, approximation and error estimates; implement adaptive mesh-error assessment on triangular elliptic problems.

practice: Prove an energy and discretization error estimate and test predicted rates with manufactured solutions and adaptive refinement.

includes: Deformation, stress, elasticity, viscoelasticity and constitutive validation

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Analyze deformable media beyond elementary fluid models.
decks.title: Continuum Mechanics

outcomes.description: Derive material/spatial deformation maps, strain and stress transformations and balance laws; construct frame-indifferent elastic/viscoelastic laws consistent with energy and dissipation.
Derive variational elasticity and coupled continuum models, implement bounded finite-element examples and discriminate constitutive laws using loading-history data and mesh/parameter sensitivity.

practice: Fit elastic/viscoelastic constitutive alternatives and validate a deformation computation against independent loading histories.

includes: Kinetic plasma theory, damping, MHD and magnetized transport

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Analyze kinetic and magnetofluid plasma behavior.
decks.title: Kinetic Plasma Physics

outcomes.description: Derive Vlasov and moment equations from phase-space transport; calculate dielectric response and Landau damping with contour prescriptions and implement a bounded one-dimensional electrostatic particle-in-cell scheme.
Derive MHD closure and Alfvén/magnetosonic modes, analyze stated stability and collisional transport models and validate conservation, resolution and closure limits.

practice: Implement particle deposition, field solution and leapfrog pushing; compare damping with kinetic and fluid predictions.

excludes: Quantum gravity and exhaustive Standard Model phenomenology
includes: Relativistic fields, quantization, propagators and perturbative renormalization

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Calculate introductory relativistic quantum-field observables.
decks.title: Quantum Field Theory

outcomes.description: Derive scalar, Dirac and electromagnetic field equations from actions; construct mode expansions, commutation/anticommutation relations and propagators using canonical and discretized Gaussian path-integral methods.

Derive Wick expansion and Feynman rules, calculate tree-level amplitudes and a scalar one-loop correction, and apply explicit regularization/renormalization conditions while checking symmetries and dimensions.

practice: Derive a tree-level cross section and renormalized scalar one-loop observable, separating regulator dependence from physical parameters.

includes: Second quantization, Green functions, response and collective order

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Analyze interacting quantum matter.
decks.title: Many-Body Physics

outcomes.description: Construct second-quantized lattice/continuum Hamiltonians; derive noninteracting Green functions, Wick contractions and bounded perturbative/Hartree-Fock approximations.
Derive linear-response and spectral observables and representative BCS or spin-wave theories; compare quasiparticle, mean-field and correlation predictions against scattering/transport evidence.

practice: Calculate a spectral or response function and test a collective-order approximation against limiting cases and published-style data.

includes: Atomic transitions, coherent driving, lasers and quantum-optical measurements

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Connect light-matter dynamics with optical evidence.
decks.title: Atomic and Quantum Optics

outcomes.description: Derive driven two-level and optical-Bloch equations with stated relaxation models; calculate Rabi oscillations, line shapes, selection rules and laser gain/threshold.
Construct coherent/Fock-state and photon-correlation predictions; analyze interferometric, lifetime and antibunching measurements with detector response and classical alternative tests.

practice: Fit coherent-drive and photon-counting data and justify whether nonclassical claims survive background and detector corrections.

includes: Electrode kinetics, transport, interfacial charge and electrochemical inference

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Infer transport and interfacial mechanisms from electrical signals.
decks.title: Electrochemistry and Interfaces

outcomes.description: Derive bounded Butler-Volmer/Tafel, steady diffusion-layer and double-layer circuit models; calculate overpotential, limiting flux and charging with explicit assumptions.
Fit voltammetry/impedance using documented tools; distinguish kinetic, transport and capacitive effects and assess corrosion, battery or electrocatalytic design tradeoffs.

practice: Analyze a cell under potential and frequency perturbations and discriminate mechanisms through residuals and independent controls.

includes: Stereoselective synthesis, pericyclic/catalytic transformations and route validation

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Design and substantiate multistep syntheses.
decks.title: Advanced Synthesis

outcomes.description: Plan convergent routes using stereoselective carbon-carbon construction, taught frontier-orbital/pericyclic rules and organo-/metal-catalytic transformations.
Compare mechanistic/spectral evidence for identity and selectivity; optimize bounded synthesis using controls, mass balance and kinetics and justify safety/sustainability tradeoffs.

practice: Defend competing routes and execute or reconstruct a supervised short sequence with purity, identity and waste evidence.

includes: Structure-reactivity relations, isotope effects and physical-organic inference

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Discriminate molecular reaction mechanisms quantitatively.
decks.title: Physical Organic Chemistry

outcomes.description: Derive transition-state/activation parameter relations under stated statistical assumptions; analyze Hammett, Brønsted, solvent and kinetic-isotope correlations and their breakdown.
Combine stereochemical, crossover, trapping, kinetic and thermodynamic evidence to distinguish concerted, stepwise and competing pathways; design falsifying rather than confirmatory experiments.

practice: Infer competing mechanisms from substituent/isotope datasets and propose a minimal discriminating experiment set.

includes: Organometallic bonding, catalytic cycles and mechanistic evidence

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Explain and test inorganic catalytic mechanisms.
decks.title: Inorganic Chemistry and Catalysis

outcomes.description: Construct orbital/electron-count descriptions and predict oxidative addition, reductive elimination, insertion, elimination and ligand-exchange pathways.

Derive molecular/surface catalytic rate and selectivity models, teaching site balances and adsorption; distinguish resting states and limiting steps using isotope, spectral, kinetic and poisoning evidence.

practice: Construct competing cycles and design kinetic and spectroscopic tests distinguishing them.

includes: Working electronic calculations, geometry optimization and validation

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Use bounded molecular calculations before many-body theory.
decks.title: Computational Chemistry

outcomes.description: Implement an orbital secular model and operate documented mean-field/DFT tools using explicitly taught basis, charge, spin, SCF and geometry-convergence settings and assumptions.
Compare energies, geometries and harmonic frequencies with experiment; test basis, conformer, spin and convergence sensitivity and distinguish numerical convergence from model validity.

practice: Run and audit a conformer/spectrum comparison, including reproducible inputs and intentionally failed convergence cases.

includes: Hartree-Fock, density-functional/correlation models and potential-energy surfaces

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Derive and validate many-electron approximations.
decks.title: Electronic Structure Methods

outcomes.description: Derive Slater-determinant Hartree-Fock and generalized SCF equations; implement restricted SCF using supplied integrals and explain DFT, perturbative and configuration-interaction correlation approximations.
Calculate geometries, frequencies and reaction paths with documented tools; distinguish basis, correlation, functional, spin and convergence errors against independent evidence.

practice: Implement minimal-basis Hartree-Fock and benchmark a reaction energy across controlled approximation levels.

includes: Spin dynamics, multidimensional NMR and time-resolved molecular spectroscopy

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Derive spectroscopic experiments and infer molecular dynamics.
decks.title: Advanced Molecular Spectroscopy

outcomes.description: Develop density-operator spin notation, rotating frames and pulse propagators; derive two-spin echo/COSY/HSQC pathways, simulate finite Fourier acquisition and analyze relaxation and artifacts.

Model pump-probe, fluorescence and exchange signals using coupled kinetic equations and instrument-response convolution; fit global spectra/time courses and assess resolution, identifiability and competing mechanisms.

practice: Implement a two-spin pulse experiment and compare kinetic hypotheses against response-convolved time-resolved spectra.

includes: Advanced separations, tandem detection, chemometrics and method validation

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Design defensible chemical measurement workflows.
decks.title: Advanced Analytical Chemistry

outcomes.description: Derive plate/retention and van-Deemter models with stated transport assumptions; design LC/GC/electrophoretic separations and tandem-MS acquisition and distinguish coelution, fragmentation and matrix suppression.

Construct multivariate calibration and designed method-optimization experiments; assess traceability, selectivity, limits, recovery, drift and interlaboratory uncertainty using independent validation data.

practice: Develop a mixture-analysis method and challenge it with blinded matrix, concentration and instrument-shift samples.

includes: Chain statistics, polymer solutions, phase behavior and rheology

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Derive polymer structure-property relationships.
decks.title: Polymer Physical Chemistry

outcomes.description: Derive ideal-chain dimensions and entropic elasticity; analyze excluded-volume scaling and Flory-Huggins mixing/phase diagrams with explicit approximation limits.
Construct Rouse and bounded viscoelastic relaxation models, calculate rheological spectra and infer relaxation distributions from scattering/mechanical data with identifiability checks.

practice: Implement a bead-spring relaxation model and compare chain-size and rheological predictions with independent measurements.

includes: Molecular dynamics, Monte Carlo, force fields and free-energy estimation

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Sample molecular systems and infer equilibrium properties.
decks.title: Molecular Simulation

outcomes.description: Implement pair forces, periodic boundaries, neighbor lists, velocity-Verlet and Metropolis moves; derive detailed balance locally and assess ensembles, thermostats, conservation, equilibration and autocorrelation.
Derive free-energy perturbation and umbrella-reweighting estimators; quantify overlap, finite-size, sampling and force-field uncertainty using independent structural/thermodynamic validation.

practice: Implement a molecular fluid and estimate a free-energy difference with replicate trajectories and overlap/force-field sensitivity studies.

includes: Experimental structural biology, inverse representations and interaction assays

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Infer biomolecular structures and interactions from measurements.
decks.title: Structural Biology

outcomes.description: Relate reciprocal-space intensities, projection images and NMR restraints to three-dimensional coordinates using taught discrete Fourier sums and forward models; use documented crystallographic/cryo-EM/restraint tools and assess phases, resolution, overfitting and ensemble ambiguity.

Design purification and binding/stability assays using taught chromatography, equilibrium occupancy, calorimetric and fluorescence response models; infer affinity, stoichiometry and conformational change with controls.

practice: Reconstruct or refine a small supplied structural dataset with documented tools and challenge its model using withheld data and orthogonal binding evidence.

includes: Quantitative imaging, signaling and causal cellular research

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Design mechanistic cell and developmental investigations.
decks.title: Cellular and Developmental Research

outcomes.description: Use documented segmentation/tracking after learning thresholding, connected components and assignment procedures; quantify localization, trajectories and lineages with artifact/uncertainty checks.
Integrate timed perturbations, rescue, live imaging and molecular readouts to distinguish signaling, mechanical and fate mechanisms; justify organism choice and welfare/consent tradeoffs.

practice: Audit live-cell image analysis and design a factorial perturbation study with quantified competing predictions.

includes: Biochemical networks, flux, regulation and system identification

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Construct and test mechanistic biological networks.
decks.title: Systems Biology

outcomes.description: Construct stoichiometric matrices and mass-action/enzyme ODEs for metabolism and regulation; analyze conservation, flux null spaces, feedback, bistability and oscillation.
Fit dynamic parameters with documented optimizers, implement sensitivity equations/profile likelihoods and design perturbations distinguishing structural and practical nonidentifiability.

practice: Implement and fit a regulatory ODE model and design a measurement resolving demonstrated parameter ambiguity.

excludes: Every omics platform and de novo folding algorithm
includes: Single-cell/multi-omics, sequence models and structural interpretation

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Infer biological structure and function from molecular data.
decks.title: Advanced Bioinformatics

outcomes.description: Construct count and latent-variable models for bulk/single-cell data; account for batch/missingness and integrate expression, accessibility and sequence without equating clusters and cell identities.

Implement sequence HMM forward/backward inference; use documented protein-structure/interaction tools with coordinate/confidence interpretation and validate functional hypotheses against independent experiments and leakage-aware benchmarks.

practice: Reanalyze multi-omics data and implement a sequence model, separating computational confidence from experimental mechanism validation.

includes: Conductance dynamics, neural circuits, point processes and coding

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Model neural dynamics and infer representations.
decks.title: Computational Neuroscience

outcomes.description: Derive membrane/gating equations; implement conductance-based neurons and excitatory/inhibitory networks; analyze excitability, equilibria, oscillations and explicit plasticity rules.
Derive conditional-intensity likelihood from time bins, fit encoding/decoding models and calculate taught entropy/mutual-information measures with sampling bias and held-out checks.

practice: Implement a conductance circuit and fit spike encoding, comparing mechanistic, predictive and intervention evidence.

includes: Eco-evolutionary feedback, spatial models and hierarchical field inference

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Connect ecological/evolutionary theory to imperfect field evidence.
decks.title: Ecological and Evolutionary Research

outcomes.description: Derive invasion-fitness and coupled trait/population models; implement patch and individual-based stochastic models and compare deterministic, stochastic and scale-dependent predictions.
Construct hierarchical demographic/environmental/genetic models, evaluate posterior predictions and design monitoring or experiments distinguishing eco-evolutionary mechanisms.

practice: Fit an integrated population model and defend a feasible, ethically justified design separating competing spatial/evolutionary mechanisms.

includes: Host-microbe mechanisms, immune repertoires and causal research

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Design mechanistic host-microbe and immune investigations.
decks.title: Infection and Immunity Research

outcomes.description: Construct testable models of invasion, microbial competition, immune evasion, tolerance and memory; interpret repertoire and single-cell assay evidence with explicit sampling/selection limits.
Design controlled perturbation, co-culture, neutralization and longitudinal immune studies; distinguish host and microbial mechanisms and justify welfare, biosafety, consent and translational limits.

practice: Analyze a curated host-microbe perturbation dataset and defend discriminating experiments using nonpathogenic surrogates or existing evidence.

excludes: Agronomic licensure and unrestricted field release
includes: Plant development, stress physiology, symbiosis and research design

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Investigate plant mechanisms across molecular and organismal scales.
decks.title: Plant Research

outcomes.description: Connect hormonal/developmental networks, source-sink relations, photosynthetic regulation, nutrient symbioses and stress acclimation to measurable plant phenotypes and competing mechanisms.

Design factorial genotype-environment experiments using gas exchange, fluorescence, isotope/transport readouts and molecular perturbations with taught assay models; assess developmental timing, chamber effects and ecological release consequences.

practice: Analyze a genotype-by-environment experiment and design orthogonal physiological and molecular tests of a stress-response mechanism.

excludes: Every single-molecule instrument and folding algorithm
includes: Biomolecular ensembles, allostery, kinetic states and structural inverse inference

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Infer biomolecular mechanisms from ensemble-sensitive evidence.
decks.title: Structural Biophysics

outcomes.description: Derive partition-function models of folding, binding and allostery and finite-state kinetic transition models; connect microscopic states to bulk and single-molecule observables.

Fit structural restraints and fluorescence/force/kinetic observations using explicit noise and state models; quantify degeneracy, model selection and predictive validation against held-out perturbations.

practice: Infer a conformational-state model from complementary structural and kinetic data and design a perturbation distinguishing equally good fits.
